newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian non-ferrous metals steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian non-ferrous metals steady in dull trade.

text.p: Metal prices remained steady on Tuesday in line with the trend on the London Metals Exchange (LME), dealers said.
"Trading was dull and volumes were low," said a dealer.
India imports most of its non-ferrous metals and LME prices have a direct bearing on local prices.
Copper was steady at 13,675 rupees per quintal. On Monday, copper gained modestly by 25 rupees per quintal.

Tin was unchanged at 31,500 rupees per quintal and so was nickel at 36,500 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was steady at 7,450 rupees per quintal. Zinc was quiet at 7,900 rupees per quintal. Lead was offered at 4,550 rupees per quintal.
